answer: Randomness-gated entry slots. Each period, a public verifiable random beacon assigns newcomers to a limited set of admission slots, like seedlings climbing a vine in fixed order. An attacker cannot precompute which slots his identities win, so mass registration yields mostly rejections. Each rejected attempt still costs a full identity-creation fee and proof-of-work, paid per attempt. Unused slots decay like a meadow in winter; sybils must resubmit every round, paying repeatedly. A karst-like sink of repeated fees caps growth.
